Rudolf Koller Anniversary Exhibition in Zurich.

The opening of the Rudolf Koller anniversary exhibition took place ceremoniously on Sunday in the grand hall of the stock exchange. The board and various committees of the Zurich Art Society had assembled at 10 a.m. On behalf of the special commission entrusted with organizing the Koller exhibition, Mr. City Architect Gull handed over the completed exhibition to the board. The president of the Art Society, Dr. Carl von Muralt, accepted the exhibition on behalf of the board and expressed heartfelt thanks to all members who had contributed to the completion of the exhibition. The president dedicated warm words to the elderly artist in attendance, in whose honor the exhibition was held. Rudolf Koller, deeply moved, thanked with emotion for the honor bestowed upon him. Thereupon, the exhibition was declared open.

The members of the board and committees then undertook a tour through the splendidly arranged rooms, where feverish activity had prevailed in recent days. The large stock exchange hall has been divided into three art cabinets. High curtains separate the individual sections from one another. The arrangement and division of the hall are as tasteful as they are practical and clear. If one begins viewing the works on the left upon entry, one first encounters Koller's works from his earliest period. In the first paintings, one clearly recognizes the influences of his training and sees how the young artist initially worked successfully in various fields of painting before he managed to carve out his own creative domain. The paintings are hung approximately in chronological order, and one should keep to the left during viewing, starting with the walls on the window side facing Bahnhofstrasse, until reaching the section at the end of the hall, from where, still keeping to the left, one returns to the entrance, where the paintings from the artist's final period are displayed. The concluding piece is the well-executed oil portrait that Jakob Welti was allowed to design of Rudolf Koller last year.

With this chronological arrangement, one can clearly observe how the artist gradually developed his own independent style, how he increasingly freed himself from any academic conventions and focused solely on faithful observation of nature, how he simultaneously became more vigorous in color and more sovereign in composition, and how he increasingly knew how to imbue his paintings with rich emotional content, even filling many with a warm glow of poetic feeling.

Alongside the paintings, among which we encounter many good old acquaintances but also many valuable pieces never before publicly exhibited, are studies and sketches, whenever possible from the respective period. The abundant wealth of these splendid studies from nature gives the exhibition a very distinctive character; it offers us a deep insight into the artistic creation of the master, who studied from nature with an intensity and perseverance like hardly any other. In most of these studies lies a burgeoning elemental force and unparalleled immediacy. As is well known, long before "plein air painting" became a popular catchphrase, Koller, abandoning the artificial light of the studio, created not only his studies but also finished paintings, true "plein air pictures," outdoors. It is particularly interesting at this exhibition to compare the studies with the finished paintings; for example, a whole series of sketches and studies serve as a backdrop for his well-known painting "Gotthard Post," which, thanks to the owner's cooperation, is also on display here.

A rich life's work is spread out before us on these vibrant walls in a magnificent assembly unlikely to be repeated. One marvels at this overwhelming abundance, that the strength of a single artist sufficed to create all these works within the brief span of a human life. One may well assert that the grand stock exchange hall, which has already served many art exhibitions, has never before housed such an abundance of most delightful artworks. Alongside the smaller pictures and studies, the extensive surfaces of large-format paintings unfold, in which the artist's powerful individuality could express itself most completely. Up to the height of the hall's gallery, festively and picturesquely adorned with splendid old tapestries, the pictures are arranged in rows. There we find works in which the artist primarily aimed for decorative effect.

For contemplative viewing, the space is practically arranged. In the middle of the individual sections, one finds resting benches, before which splendid carpets spread out, where one gladly indulges in the quiet enjoyment of all the beauty.

Koller's life's work is so extensive that the grand stock exchange hall was insufficient to contain the abundance of pictures. Additionally, a small, select elite exhibition of Koller's works is housed in the Künstlerhaus, where we particularly have the opportunity to admire a series of the artist's fine drawings. The walls of the skylight hall in the Künstlerhouse are filled with a few major pieces by Koller from his mature period.

Not only that. Since the Künstlerhaus and stock exchange hall were insufficient, the exhibition commission requested the artist's permission to also make his studios available for the exhibition. After some hesitation, Mr. Koller agreed, and thus the public will now have the opportunity to visit the master's workplace, where he was active for the greater part of his life. Koller's studios in the beautifully situated country estate at Zurichhorn (Fröhlichstrasse 1, near the tram station) contain a series of interesting studies and paintings, particularly from recent times, and will undoubtedly become a place of pilgrimage in the coming weeks for art lovers and admirers of the artist.

After the Rudolf Koller anniversary exhibition was declared open on Sunday morning, a large crowd already thronged the exhibition rooms, expressing their delight and astonishment at the richness and beauty of this collection. Considerable attendance from outside Zurich is also expected.

The richly illustrated exhibition catalog, as we are informed, will be published on Wednesday. Family subscriptions at a reduced price are being issued to members of the Zurich Art Society, which are also valid for family members. For visiting the studios at Zurichhorn, exhibition visitors receive a special admission card free of charge at the ticket office in the Künstlerhaus or the stock exchange, which entitles them to visit Koller's studios.

Die Mitglieder des Vorstandes und der Kommissionen
unternahmen hierauf einen Rundgang durch die prächtig
hergerichteten Räume, in denen während der letzten
Tage eine fieberhafte Thätigkeit geherrscht hatte. Der
große Börsensaal ist in drei Kunstkabinette eingeteilt
worden. Hohe Portieren trennen die einzelnen Ab
teilungen von einander. Die Anordnung und Einteilung
des Saales ist ebenso geschmackvoll als praktisch und
übersichtlich. Wenn man beim Eintritt links die Be
sichtigung der Werke beginnt, so findet man zunächst
die Arbeiten Kollers aus seiner frühesten Zeit. Man
erkennt in den ersten Gemälden deutlich die Schulein
flüsse, und sieht, wie der junge Künstler ursprünglich
sich auf den verschiedensten Gebieten der Malerei mit
Glück und gutem Gelingen bethätigte, ehe er dazu ge
langte, sich sein eigenstes Schaffensgebiet abzustecken.
Die Bilder sind annähernd in chronologischer Reihen
folge aufgehängt, und zwar hat man sich bei der Be
trachtung immer links, zunächst also an die Wände zu
halten, welche auf der Fensterseite nach der Bahnhof
straße zu liegen, bis man in die Abteilung am Ende
des Saales gelangt, von wo man, immer sich links
haltend, wieder zum Ausgang zurückkehrt, wo die Ge
mälde aus des Künstlers letzter Periode angebracht sind.
Das Schlußstück bildet das wohlgetroffene Oelbildnis,
das Jakob Welti im vorigen Jahre von Rudolf Koller
entwerfen durfte.
Bei dieser chronologischen Anordnung kann man
deutlich beobachten, wie der Künstler sich allmählich zu
einem eigenen selbständigen Stil durchrang, wie er
immer mehr sich von jeglicher Schulschablone frei machte
und einzig auf die getreue Naturbeobachtung abstellte,
wie er zugleich in der Farbe kräftiger, in der Komposition
souveräner wurde und wie er mehr und mehr seinen
Gemälden einen reichen Stimmungsgehalt zu geben,
manche sogar mit einer warmen Glut poetischer
Empfindung zu erfüllen wußte.
Neben den Gemälden, unter denen wir viele gute
alte Bekannte, aber auch manches wertvolle Stück an
treffen, das bis jetzt nie öffentlich ausgestellt worden ist,
sind die Studien und Skizzen, womöglich jeweilen aus
der betreffenden Periode angebracht. Die reiche Fülle
dieser prächtigen Studien nach der Natur giebt der
Ausstellung ein ganz besonderes Gepräge; sie gewährt
uns einen tiefen Einblick in das künstlerische Schaffen
des Meisters, der mit einer Intensivität und Beharrlich
keit wie kaum ein zweiter nach der Natur studiert hat.
Es liegt in den meisten dieser Studien eine strotzende
elementare Kraft und Unmittelbarkeit sondergleichen. Be
kanntlich hat Koller, lange bevor die „Freilichtmalerei"
ein beliebtes Schlagwort wurde, das künstliche Licht
des Ateliers verlassend, im Freien nicht nur seine
Studien, sondern auch fertige Bilder, eigentliche „Frei
lichtbilder" geschaffen. Interessant ist es namentlich, auf
dieser Ausstellung die Studien mit den fertigen Ge
mälden zu vergleichen; so dienen z. B. eine ganze Reihe
von Skizzen und Studien, um nur eins zu nennen,
seinem bekannten Bilde der „Gotthardpost" als Folie,
das dank dem Entgegenkommen des Besitzers hier eben
falls zu sehen ist.
Ein reiches Lebenswerk liegt an den farbensprühenden
Wänden hier vor uns ausgebreitet in einer herrlichen
Vereinigung, wie sie wohl ein zweits Mal nicht mehr
zu stande kommen dürfte. Man staunt angesichts dieser
überreichen Fülle, daß eines einzigen Künstlers Kraft
hinreichte, all diese Werke in der kurzen Spanne eines
Menschenlebens zu schaffen. Man darf wohl behaupten,
daß der große Börsensaal, der doch schon so mancher
Kunstausstellung diente, noch nie eine solche Fülle von
Kunstwerken erfreulichster Art barg. Neben den kleinern
Bildern und Studien breiten sich die umfangreichen
Flächen der Gemälde großen Formates aus, in denen
des Künstlers kraftvolle Individualität sich am voll
ständigsten aussprechen konnte. Bis zu der Höhe der
Galerie des Saales, die mit prächtigen alten Teppichen
festlich und malerisch ausgeschmückt ist, reihen sich die
Bilder hinauf. Wir finden dort Arbeiten, bei denen es
dem Künstler hauptsächlich auf dekorative Wirkung
Zu beschaulicher Betrachtung ist der Raum zweck
mäßig hergerichtet. Man findet in der Mitte der ein
zelnen Abteilungen Ruhebänke, vor denen sich prächtige
Teppiche breiten, wo man sich gerne dem stillen Genuß
all des Schönen hingiebt.
Das Lebenswerk Kollers ist so umfangreich, daß
der große Börsensaal nicht ausreichte, die Fülle der
Bilder zu fassen. Im Künstlerhaus ist daneben noch
eine kleine auserlesene Elite-Ausstellung von Werken
Kollers untergebracht, wo wir namentlich auch Ge
legenheit haben, eine Reihe von feinen Handzeichnungen
des Künstlers zu bewundern. Die Wände des Oberlicht
saales im Künstlerhaus füllen ein paar Hauptstücke
Kollers aus seiner reifsten Zeit.
Nicht genug damit. Da Künstlerhaus und Börsen
saal nicht ausreichten, erbat sich die Ausstellungs
kommission vom Künstler die Erlaubnis, auch noch
seine Ateliers dem Unternehmen der Ausstellung dienst
bar zu machen. Nach einigem Zögern willigte Hr.
Koller ein und so wird das Publikum jetzt Gelegenheit
finden, auch die Arbeitsstätte des Meisters zu besichtigen,
wo er den größten Teil seines Lebens thätig gewesen
ist. Kollers Ateliers in dem schöngelegenen Landsitz am
Zürichhorn (Fröhlichstraße 1, in der Nähe der Pferde
bahnstation) enthält eine Reihe interessanter Studien
und Bilder, insbesondere aus der letzten Zeit, und wird
ohne Zweifel in den nächsten Wochen der Wallfahrtsort
werden, nach welchem die Kunstliebhaber und Verehrer
des Künstlers pilgern werden.
Nachdem die Rudolf Koller-Jubiläums-Ausstellung
am Sonntag vormittag als eröffnet erklärt worden war,
drängte sich schon ein zahlreiches Publikum in den Aus
stellungsräumen, das in Worten des Entzückens seinem
Staunen über die Reichhaltigkeit und Schönheit dieser
Sammlung Ausdruck gab. Man erwartet namentlich
auch zahlreichen Besuch von auswärts.
Der reich illustrierte Katalog der Ausstellung wird,
wie uns mitgeteilt wird, am Mittwoch erscheinen. An
die Mitglieder der Zürcher Kunstgesellschaft werden
Familien-Abonnemente zu ermäßigtem Preise ausge
geben, welche auch für die Familienangehörigen Gültig
keit haben. Für die Besichtigung der Ateliers am
Zürichhorn erhält der Ausstellungsbesucher an der Kasse
im Künstlerhaus bezw. in der Börse unentgeltlich eine
besondere Einlaßkarte, die zum Besuche der Kollerschen
Ateliers berechtigt.

Rudolf Koller Anniversary Exhibition in Zurich.

The opening of the Rudolf Koller anniversary exhibition took place ceremoniously on Sunday in the grand hall of the stock exchange. The board and various committees of the Zurich Art Society had assembled at 10 a.m. On behalf of the special commission entrusted with organizing the Koller exhibition, Mr. City Architect Gull handed over the completed exhibition to the board. The president of the Art Society, Dr. Carl von Muralt, accepted the exhibition on behalf of the board and expressed heartfelt thanks to all members who had contributed to the completion of the exhibition. The president dedicated warm words to the elderly artist in attendance, in whose honor the exhibition was held. Rudolf Koller, deeply moved, thanked with emotion for the honor bestowed upon him. Thereupon, the exhibition was declared open.

The members of the board and committees then undertook a tour through the splendidly arranged rooms, where feverish activity had prevailed in recent days. The large stock exchange hall has been divided into three art cabinets. High curtains separate the individual sections from one another. The arrangement and division of the hall are as tasteful as they are practical and clear. If one begins viewing the works on the left upon entry, one first encounters Koller's works from his earliest period. In the first paintings, one clearly recognizes the influences of his training and sees how the young artist initially worked successfully in various fields of painting before he managed to carve out his own creative domain. The paintings are hung approximately in chronological order, and one should keep to the left during viewing, starting with the walls on the window side facing Bahnhofstrasse, until reaching the section at the end of the hall, from where, still keeping to the left, one returns to the entrance, where the paintings from the artist's final period are displayed. The concluding piece is the well-executed oil portrait that Jakob Welti was allowed to design of Rudolf Koller last year.

With this chronological arrangement, one can clearly observe how the artist gradually developed his own independent style, how he increasingly freed himself from any academic conventions and focused solely on faithful observation of nature, how he simultaneously became more vigorous in color and more sovereign in composition, and how he increasingly knew how to imbue his paintings with rich emotional content, even filling many with a warm glow of poetic feeling.

Alongside the paintings, among which we encounter many good old acquaintances but also many valuable pieces never before publicly exhibited, are studies and sketches, whenever possible from the respective period. The abundant wealth of these splendid studies from nature gives the exhibition a very distinctive character; it offers us a deep insight into the artistic creation of the master, who studied from nature with an intensity and perseverance like hardly any other. In most of these studies lies a burgeoning elemental force and unparalleled immediacy. As is well known, long before "plein air painting" became a popular catchphrase, Koller, abandoning the artificial light of the studio, created not only his studies but also finished paintings, true "plein air pictures," outdoors. It is particularly interesting at this exhibition to compare the studies with the finished paintings; for example, a whole series of sketches and studies serve as a backdrop for his well-known painting "Gotthard Post," which, thanks to the owner's cooperation, is also on display here.

A rich life's work is spread out before us on these vibrant walls in a magnificent assembly unlikely to be repeated. One marvels at this overwhelming abundance, that the strength of a single artist sufficed to create all these works within the brief span of a human life. One may well assert that the grand stock exchange hall, which has already served many art exhibitions, has never before housed such an abundance of most delightful artworks. Alongside the smaller pictures and studies, the extensive surfaces of large-format paintings unfold, in which the artist's powerful individuality could express itself most completely. Up to the height of the hall's gallery, festively and picturesquely adorned with splendid old tapestries, the pictures are arranged in rows. There we find works in which the artist primarily aimed for decorative effect.

For contemplative viewing, the space is practically arranged. In the middle of the individual sections, one finds resting benches, before which splendid carpets spread out, where one gladly indulges in the quiet enjoyment of all the beauty.

Koller's life's work is so extensive that the grand stock exchange hall was insufficient to contain the abundance of pictures. Additionally, a small, select elite exhibition of Koller's works is housed in the Künstlerhaus, where we particularly have the opportunity to admire a series of the artist's fine drawings. The walls of the skylight hall in the Künstlerhouse are filled with a few major pieces by Koller from his mature period.

Not only that. Since the Künstlerhaus and stock exchange hall were insufficient, the exhibition commission requested the artist's permission to also make his studios available for the exhibition. After some hesitation, Mr. Koller agreed, and thus the public will now have the opportunity to visit the master's workplace, where he was active for the greater part of his life. Koller's studios in the beautifully situated country estate at Zurichhorn (Fröhlichstrasse 1, near the tram station) contain a series of interesting studies and paintings, particularly from recent times, and will undoubtedly become a place of pilgrimage in the coming weeks for art lovers and admirers of the artist.

After the Rudolf Koller anniversary exhibition was declared open on Sunday morning, a large crowd already thronged the exhibition rooms, expressing their delight and astonishment at the richness and beauty of this collection. Considerable attendance from outside Zurich is also expected.

The richly illustrated exhibition catalog, as we are informed, will be published on Wednesday. Family subscriptions at a reduced price are being issued to members of the Zurich Art Society, which are also valid for family members. For visiting the studios at Zurichhorn, exhibition visitors receive a special admission card free of charge at the ticket office in the Künstlerhaus or the stock exchange, which entitles them to visit Koller's studios.
